title: HostedAPI p98 latency creep and KV locking retrospective
summary: Between 2026-07-27 17:30 UTC and 2026-07-28 03:10 UTC we observed a sustained increase in p98 token latency for the hosted API for short-response chat requests. P50 and median responsiveness remained within SLOs; the increase manifested almost exclusively in the p95-p99 tail and correlated with elevated KV cache lock wait times on a subset of inference workers. The event reduced effective throughput for tail-sensitive clients and triggered several customer-reported timeouts. This doc describes detection, root cause analysis, immediate actions, and follow-ups.
detection_and_alerting: Alerting: automatic p99 latency alert (threshold 1.8s) fired at 2026-07-27 17:39 UTC. On-call page triggered. Additional customer Slack reports came in at 18:05 UTC for repeated streaming stalls. Observability: tracing showed long idle periods inside the 'kv_cache.fetch' span. Telemetry: KV lock contention metric (kv.lock_wait_ms) climbed from baseline ~2ms to sustained 40-200ms on ~12% of worker pods.
timeline:
2026-07-27 17:30 UTC - first rise in p98 detected in dashboard
2026-07-27 17:39 UTC - p99 alert fires; SRE oncall paged
2026-07-27 17:45 UTC - initial triage: traffic steady, no infra scaling events; sampling traces show locking
2026-07-27 18:10 UTC - mitigation attempt #1: toggle adaptive-prefetch flag off for candidate pool (quick config flip)
2026-07-27 18:22 UTC - p98 partially recovered in flagged pool but persisted cluster-wide
2026-07-27 19:05 UTC - mitigate #2: increase KV cache worker threads from 8 -> 12 on hot pools (rolling restart)
2026-07-27 20:20 UTC - observed transient improvement; tail still elevated during short-burst load patterns
2026-07-27 23:00 UTC - deploy temporary circuit-breaker that avoids heavy KV-prefetch for requests <64 tokens
2026-07-28 00:30 UTC - tail metrics stabilized to near-SLO for majority of traffic; monitoring in watch mode
2026-07-28 03:10 UTC - incident declared resolved; follow-up investigation commenced
impact:
- Increased p98/p99 token latency for short chat and single-shot generation requests for ~9 hours
- Customer-facing errors: ~0.8% increase in client-visible timeouts; three paying customers reported elevated request times and one escalated to CS
- Internal: increased CPU and lock contention on a subset of inference workers; temporary reduction in effective throughput for tail-sensitive workloads
- No data loss, no model degradation, and no cross-region failover triggered
root_cause: A change to the adaptive prefetch heuristic (rolled out 2026-07-26 as part of PR #1882) increased aggressive KV prefetch attempts for predicted-prefixes. On heavily-sharded hot keys the prefetcher started issuing concurrent KV writes/reads that caused mutex contention in our in-process KV cache layer. The contention presented as long lock wait times which only affected requests that touched the hot prefix path (short-response chat flows). The rollout lacked sufficient throttling for concurrent prefetches and did not exercise tail-latency scenarios in the canary profile.
contributing_factors: Adaptive prefetch rollout did not include a conservative concurrency cap for hot-key paths
Canary traffic profile didn’t include high-frequency short bursts observed in production customers
KV cache instrumentation surfaced average latencies but lacked high-resolution per-key lock histograms
Operational runbook did not have a fast kill-switch for this specific prefetch flag
immediate_mitigation:
1) Rolled back the aggressive prefetch defaults in the runtime config for all pools by 18:10 UTC.
2) Increased KV cache worker threads in the hot pool and triggered rolling restarts to drain lock queues.
3) Deployed a temporary circuit-breaker that bypassed prefetch for requests with estimated output tokens < 64.
These mitigations reduced lock wait times and brought p98 closer to SLO within ~2 hours.
permanent_fixes: Revert PR #1882 until a safer concurrency control is implemented for prefetch (complete)
Add a per-prefix concurrent-prefetch limit and exponential backoff for retrying prefetches
Enhance KV cache to expose per-key lock wait histograms and an alert when >5% of keys have wait >50ms
Add tail-scenario test in canary harness that replays short-burst traffic from production replay traces
Introduce a targeted feature-flag kill-switch that can be toggled without a rolling restart

lessons_learned:
- Prefetch/optimization features must be gated behind conservative concurrency controls and should not be enabled cluster-wide without tail-focused canaries.
- Tail-specific telemetry (per-key lock histograms) is critical to detect contention early.
- Small config flips can have global tail effects; we need a fast, low-friction kill-switch for runtime heuristics.
- Customer traffic shapes matter: canaries must reflect short-burst, high-frequency patterns in addition to steady-state loads.
